Workflows we build

What changes, workflow by workflow.

  • OM, rent roll and T-12 extraction

    Excel models · CoStar and CREXi exports · Dealpath
    Today
    An analyst types unit mixes, in-place rents and trailing financials into the model before any real underwriting starts.
    What we build
    Upload the deal package. Unit mix, rents, T-12 line items and key OM terms land in your model's input tabs, each value linked to its source page, with totals reconciled before anything is accepted.

  • Underwriting and IC memo drafts

    Excel · Word and PDF templates · Dealpath
    Today
    Memos are built by copying from the model, the OM and market comps, then rebuilt when numbers move.
    What we build
    A first draft in your own template, generated from approved model outputs and source documents. The analyst edits and signs off, and every figure ties back to the model.

  • Lease abstraction

    Yardi · MRI Software · AppFolio
    Today
    Critical dates and clauses are read out of scanned leases one at a time.
    What we build
    Abstracts with clause-level citations for term, options, escalations, co-tenancy and expense recoveries. Flagged items go to a reviewer queue, and approved abstracts export in the format your property system takes.

  • LP onboarding, capital calls and distributions

    Juniper Square · Salesforce · DocuSign
    Today
    Subscription documents, tax forms and notices are chased by email and tracked in a spreadsheet.
    What we build
    An investor portal for subscription documents, accreditation, tax forms and e-signature, with capital call and distribution notices generated from your records.

  • Asset management reporting

    Yardi · MRI Software · AppFolio · Excel
    Today
    Monthly property reports are downloaded, re-formatted and rolled up by hand.
    What we build
    Property-level reports pulled on a schedule and rolled into a portfolio view, with variances against budget flagged for the asset manager.
How it works

Extraction you can check, with a person in the loop.

Every value carries its source. Anything that does not reconcile is held for review.

  1. Documents inUploads, email attachments, system exports.
  2. ExtractFields pulled into a fixed structure, with the source page recorded.
  3. ReviewValidation rules run. A person confirms or corrects what is flagged.
  4. System of recordApproved data lands in your model, CRM, core or fund-admin system.
  5. ReportMemos, statements and audit trails generated from approved data.

Security

How your data is handled.

Security and data handling

  • Deal documents and investor records stay in your systems. We do not keep a copy of investor PII on MonkFlow infrastructure.

  • Role-based access, so a broker, an analyst and an LP each see only what they should.

  • Every extraction, edit and approval is logged with who and when.

Questions

What firms ask us first.

Will this work with our existing Excel model?

Yes. We build to your workbook as it is: your tabs, your input cells, your naming. You do not have to move to a new modeling tool.

How do you keep extracted numbers accurate?

Three ways. Validation rules catch what should reconcile and does not, such as rent roll totals or T-12 subtotals. Every value links to its source page. And a person reviews flagged items before anything is accepted into the model.

Have you worked with commercial real estate firms before?

Our named client work so far is in wealth management, with Team Financial Strategies. For commercial real estate we have built a working land search tool for brokers, which you can see today. We would rather show you working software on your own documents than a wall of logos.

What does an engagement cost?

It depends on the workflow, the systems involved and how much review tooling your team needs. Every engagement is scoped individually, and you see a written scope and quote before any build work starts.

Not sure where to start? Start with a workflow audit.

We map one workflow and the systems around it, rank the automation opportunities, and write up scope and data handling. You decide what, if anything, to build.

Bring us your worst manual workflow.

A working session is 20 minutes with the engineer who would build it. Walk through the process, and leave with a straight answer on whether it is worth automating.
